ratings.notes: Strong multi-hop evidence with good hop distinction. Ivacaftor/Akkermansia claim plausible but answer truncated. PMIDs appear legitimate and well-contextualized.
Correctly distinguishes hops but uses only two studies. Honest about inferential gap. Lacks human evidence, ivacaftor data, and mechanistic detail. Concise but incomplete.
Excellent hop-by-hop evidence with rescue experiments, human data, and ivacaftor intervention. Well-grounded PMIDs. Strongest causal framing with gut-corrected mouse model.
Comprehensive, well-structured with clear hop separation, antibiotic rescue evidence, gut-corrected model, human ivacaftor data, and explicit mechanistic pathway summary.

result.pairwise_reason: PP010-D and PP010-C are near-equivalent in quality; PP010-D edges ahead by explicitly articulating the full mechanistic pathway (ion/water transport → selective pressure → dysbiosis → permeability → innate immune activation), including antibiotic rescue evidence, and clearly labeling inference vs. direct evidence at each hop.
